create.name: Arsha Vidya Gurukulam
create.bio:
Arsha Vidya Gurukulam is a residential centre for the traditional study of Advaita Vedanta, set in the Pocono Mountains at Saylorsburg, Pennsylvania. Swami Dayananda Saraswati started it in 1986 on the pattern of the Indian gurukulam, where students live alongside their teachers while they study, and it also goes by the name Arsha Vidya Pitham. A temple to Lord Dakshinamurti stands on the grounds, and daily worship runs alongside the classes.

Teaching rests on the Bhagavad Gita, the Upanishads and the Brahmasutras, given in English by resident acharyas in Swami Dayananda's line, among them Swami Viditatmananda, Swami Tattvavidananda and Swami Muktatmananda, with visiting teachers such as Swamini Svatmavidyananda. Sanskrit, Vedic chanting, meditation and Iyengar yoga are taught too, along with family courses, a children's camp and residential retreats, and the Vedanta classes themselves carry no fee. Gita classes on the first and third Sundays of each month are open to all without booking and are streamed live, and a guided meditation is held online twice a month. The YouTube channel carries those Sunday classes, longer courses and recordings of festival pujas.

courses.title: 2026 Thanksgiving Family Vedanta Course
courses.description: A four-day course at the Gurukulam over the Thanksgiving weekend, attended in person or watched online. Swami Muktatmananda speaks on family life in the Hindu tradition and Swami Sachidananda teaches three short morning verses on the nature of the Self.

free_resources.title: Bhagavad Gita weekend classes
free_resources.description: Two Gita sessions in the temple lecture hall on the first and third Sunday of every month, open to anyone and streamed live, followed by arati and an optional satsang over lunch.

free_resources.title: Meditation Workshop
free_resources.description: An hour of guided meditation on Zoom with Swamini Ramananda, a long-time student of Swami Dayananda, on the first and third Saturdays of the month.
